construction_markdown:
Let
\[
p(Z)=Z^{16}+Z^5+Z^3+Z^2+1,
\qquad F=\mathbb F_2[Z]/(p),
\]
and put \(\alpha=Z\bmod p\). Write \(z\in F\) uniquely as \(z=\sum_{i=0}^{15}z_i\alpha^i\).

Define
\[
A=\left\{\sum_{i=0}^{14}a_i\alpha^i:a_i\in\mathbb F_2\right\},
\qquad Y=\mathbb F_2^{15},
\]
each ordered by binary-integer order. Let \(M=F[X]_{\le64}\), ordered using the basis \(\{\alpha^iX^j:0\le i\le15,0\le j\le64\}\). Thus \(M\cong\mathbb F_2^{1040}\).

For \(y\in Y\), define
\[
h_y(z)=z_0+\sum_{i=1}^{15}z_i y_i.
\]
For every \((a,y)\in A\times Y\), define the functional
\[
\ell_{a,y}(P)=h_y(P(a))\in\mathbb F_2.
\]
Let \(G=M^*\) and
\[
D=\{\ell_{a,y}:(a,y)\in A\times Y\}\subset G.
\]
The functionals are pairwise distinct and nonzero. Hence \(\Gamma=\operatorname{Cay}(G,D)\) is a deterministic simple undirected Cayley graph of degree \(|D|=2^{30}\).

Its character code is
\[
C=\left\{c_P=(\ell_{a,y}(P))_{(a,y)\in A\times Y}:P\in M\right\},
\]
with coordinates in the displayed order. No puncturing, shortening, padding, repetition, or random choice occurs.

discussion_posts.body_markdown: For an ordered multiset `D=(d_1,…,d_n)` spanning `F_2^k`, its character code `c_a=(a·d_i)_i` has `wt(c_a)=(n-Σ_i(-1)^(a·d_i))/2`. Thus the immutable target is exactly the one-sided Cayley condition `Σ_i(-1)^(a·d_i)≤2^21` for every `a≠0`. A bipartition character with sum `-n` is harmless.
discussion_posts.subject: One-sided Cayley spectrum equals minimum distance

discussion_posts.body_markdown: If an `(m,u,2^30,λ)` relative difference set lies in an elementary abelian 2-group, write `m=2^a,u=2^s`. It has at most one point per forbidden-subgroup coset, so `a≥30`. Pair counting gives `2^30(2^30−1)=λ2^s(2^a−1)`, whence `s≤30` and `a|30`. Therefore `a=30` and the ambient dimension is `30+s≤60`. Ordinary difference sets are the `s=0` case and force only dimension 30.
discussion_posts.subject: Exact-degree relative-difference-set ceiling is k=60

discussion_posts.body_markdown: The tempting `[32768,17,16383]_2` inner code does not exist. Repeated use of the binary residual-code lemma and equality in the Griesmer bound would produce a `[9,5,4]_2` code. A parity-check matrix for the latter would require nine distinct nonzero vectors in `F_2^4` with no zero-sum triple; translating such a set by one of its members gives a disjoint set of the same size inside a 16-element group, so its size is at most eight. Consequently a dimension-17 inner/product-distance route has final dimension at most `17·61=1037`.
discussion_posts.subject: Dimension-17 half-block loophole is closed

distance_audit: For every `z∈F`, `Σ_y(-1)^{h_y(z)}` equals `2^15` for `z=0`, `−2^15` for `z=1`, and `0` otherwise.
Consequently the Cayley eigenvalue indexed by `P` is `λ_P=2^15(N_0(P)−N_1(P))`, where `N_b(P)=|{a∈A:P(a)=b}|`.
For nonconstant `P` of degree at most 64, both `N_0(P)` and `N_1(P)` are at most 64. Hence `|λ_P|≤64·2^15=2^21`.
The constant polynomial `1` gives eigenvalue `−2^30` and the all-one codeword. Every other nonzero constant gives eigenvalue zero and weight `2^29`.
Thus every nonzero word has weight at least `(2^30−2^21)/2=535822336`.
A deterministic scaled 64-root polynomial has `N_0=64,N_1=0`, attaining eigenvalue `2^21` and proving the stated distance is exact.
explicitness_audit: Repeated squaring gives `Z^(2^8)≡Z^8+Z^7+Z^3+Z` and `Z^(2^16)≡Z (mod p)`; the Euclidean remainders for `gcd(p,Z^(2^8)+Z)` end in `Z^2+1,1`. Rabin's criterion therefore certifies irreducibility.
The field basis, message basis, evaluation subset, outer ordering, inner ordering, and flattened coordinate ordering are all displayed.
If `ℓ_{a,y}=ℓ_{a',y'}`, testing constant polynomials gives `y=y'`; testing `zX` for every `z∈F` then gives `a=a'`. Also `ℓ_{a,y}(1)=1`, so no connection element is zero.
The exact-distance witness uses the first 64 elements of `A` and the first nonzero scale outside an explicitly defined forbidden set of at most 32704 elements.
The encoder uses no probabilistic object or hidden finite search.

obstructions: This construction ties, rather than exceeds, the durable under-review `k=1040` RS–RM candidate; its new contribution is the Cayley spectral certificate and scoped obstruction lemmas.
Every ordinary difference-set connection set of exact cardinality `2^30` in an elementary abelian 2-group is the degenerate whole-group case and has dimension 30.
Every classical relative-difference-set connection set of that cardinality has ambient binary dimension at most 60.

A length-32768, dimension-17 inner code cannot provide a product-distance improvement over 1040: the sole numerically viable distance 16383 is impossible, and distance at most 16382 gives final dimension at most 1037.
The Cayley graph is bipartite. Its eigenvalue `−2^30` must be treated as a second trivial eigenvalue; claiming an absolute bound for every nonprincipal character would be false.

proof_markdown:
# Cayley-character certificate for the exact 1040-dimensional code

## Theorem

There is a deterministic binary linear code with exact parameters
\[
[2^{30},1040,535{,}822{,}336]_2.
\]
Equivalently, there is a connected bipartite Cayley graph on the elementary abelian group \(\mathbb F_2^{1040}\), of degree \(2^{30}\), whose two trivial eigenvalues are \(\pm2^{30}\) and whose other eigenvalues have magnitude at most \(2^{21}\).

## Field certificate

For
\[
p(Z)=Z^{16}+Z^5+Z^3+Z^2+1,
\]
direct repeated squaring modulo \(p\) gives
\[
Z^{2^8}\equiv Z^8+Z^7+Z^3+Z,
\qquad Z^{2^{16}}\equiv Z.
\]
Moreover, the Euclidean algorithm for \(p\) and \(Z^{2^8}+Z=Z^8+Z^7+Z^3\) ends with the nonzero remainders \(Z^2+1\) and \(1\). Since 2 is the sole prime divisor of 16, Rabin's criterion proves that \(p\) is irreducible. Thus the displayed quotient is the fixed field \(F\) of order \(2^{16}\).

## Cayley set, length, and dimension

Let \(M=F[X]_{\le64}\). It has binary dimension \(65\cdot16=1040\). Define \(A,Y,h_y,\ell_{a,y}\), and \(D\subset M^*\) as in the construction.

The functionals in \(D\) are distinct. Indeed, if \(\ell_{a,y}=\ell_{a',y'}\), testing every constant polynomial \(z\in F\) shows that the coefficient vectors \((1,y)\) and \((1,y')\) define the same functional on \(F\), hence \(y=y'\). Testing the polynomials \(zX\) then gives
\[
h_y(z(a-a'))=0\quad\text{for every }z\in F.
\]
If \(a\ne a'\), multiplication by \(a-a'\) is a bijection of \(F\), contradicting that \(h_y(1)=1\). Hence \(a=a'\). Also \(\ell_{a,y}(1)=1\), so no element of \(D\) is zero. Since an elementary abelian group is its own inverse, \(D=-D\). Therefore the Cayley graph is simple and undirected, with degree
\[
|D|=|A||Y|=2^{15}2^{15}=2^{30}.
\]

The map \(P\mapsto c_P\) is binary linear. If \(c_P=0\), then for each \(a\in A\), the entire affine word \((h_y(P(a)))_{y\in Y}\) is zero. The map \(z\mapsto(h_y(z))_y\) is injective, so \(P(a)=0\) for all 32768 points of \(A\). Since \(\deg P\le64\), this forces \(P=0\). Thus the encoder is injective and \(\dim C=1040\). Equivalently, \(D\) spans \(M^*\), so the Cayley graph is connected.

## Character spectrum and distance

For \(z\in F\), affine balance gives
\[
\sum_{y\in Y}(-1)^{h_y(z)}=
\begin{cases}
2^{15},&z=0,\\
-2^{15},&z=1,\\
0,&z\notin\{0,1\}.
\end{cases}
\]
The character of \(M^*\) indexed by \(P\in M\) is \(\chi_P(\ell)=(-1)^{\ell(P)}\). Its Cayley eigenvalue is therefore
\[
\lambda_P=\sum_{a\in A}\sum_{y\in Y}(-1)^{h_y(P(a))}
=2^{15}\bigl(N_0(P)-N_1(P)\bigr).
\]
For \(P=0\), this is \(2^{30}\). For \(P=1\), it is \(-2^{30}\), displaying the bipartition. Any other nonzero constant gives zero. If \(P\) is nonconstant, both \(P\) and \(P-1\) have degree at most 64, so
\[
N_0(P)\le64,
\qquad N_1(P)\le64,
\qquad |\lambda_P|\le64\cdot2^{15}=2^{21}.
\]
Since
\[
\operatorname{wt}(c_P)=\frac{2^{30}-\lambda_P}{2},
\]
every nonzero word has weight at least
\[
\frac{2^{30}-2^{21}}2
=2^{29}-2^{20}
=535{,}822{,}336.
\]

The bound is attained. Let \(R\) be the first 64 elements of \(A\) and put
\[
g(X)=\prod_{r\in R}(X-r).
\]
For each \(a\in A\setminus R\), precisely one scalar \(\mu=g(a)^{-1}\) would make \(\mu g(a)=1\). At most 32704 of the 65535 nonzero scalars are forbidden. Choose the first permissible \(\mu\) in polynomial-basis order. Then \(P_*=\mu g\) has exactly 64 zero evaluations and no evaluation equal to 1. Hence \(\lambda_{P_*}=64\cdot2^{15}=2^{21}\), and its word has weight exactly 535822336.

## Relative-difference-set obstruction

Let \(R\) be an \((m,u,2^{30},\lambda)\) relative difference set in an elementary abelian 2-group, relative to a subgroup of order \(u\). Write \(m=2^a\) and \(u=2^s\). No two elements of \(R\) lie in the same forbidden-subgroup coset, so \(2^{30}\le2^a\) and \(a\ge30\). Counting ordered differences gives
\[
2^{30}(2^{30}-1)=\lambda2^s(2^a-1).
\]
Comparing 2-adic valuations gives \(s\le30\); after removing the powers of two, \(2^a-1\mid2^{30}-1\), hence \(a\mid30\). Thus \(a=30\) and the ambient group has dimension \(a+s\le60\). The ordinary difference-set case has \(s=0\) and dimension 30. Therefore classical difference-set flat spectra cannot approach the 1040-dimensional candidate at the exact degree.

## Dimension-17 product obstruction

The binary Griesmer bound gives \(d\le16383\) for any \([32768,17,d]_2\) code. Equality is impossible. The residual-code lemma says that a word of weight \(w<2d\) in an \([n,k,d]_2\) code produces an \([n-w,k-1,\ge d-\lfloor w/2\rfloor]_2\) residual code. Applying it to a hypothetical \([32768,17,16383]_2\) code, and using Griesmer equality at every stage, gives
\[
[16385,16,8192]_2,
[8193,15,4096]_2,
\ldots,
[9,5,4]_2.
\]
A parity-check matrix for a \([9,5,4]_2\) code would have nine distinct nonzero columns in \(\mathbb F_2^4\) with no three summing to zero. If \(S\) is such a column set and \(x\in S\), then \(S\) and \(x+S\) are disjoint, so \(2|S|\le16\), contradicting \(|S|=9\). Thus the hypothetical inner code does not exist.

Consequently every dimension-17 inner code has distance at most 16382. A product-distance proof at the target then needs outer distance at least
\[
\left\lceil\frac{535822336}{16382}\right\rceil=32708.
\]
Singleton bounds a length-32768 field-linear outer code by dimension 61, giving final binary dimension at most \(17\cdot61=1037\).

proof_steps.proof: The displayed Frobenius residues and Euclidean remainder chain satisfy Rabin's degree-16 criterion.
Constant polynomials distinguish the inner index; polynomials `zX` then distinguish the evaluation point. Every functional takes value one on the constant polynomial one.
A zero encoded word forces `P(a)=0` at all 32768 evaluation points, impossible for a nonzero polynomial of degree at most 64.
proof_steps.statement: The character code is binary linear of dimension 1040.

proof_steps.proof: The inner function is zero for symbol 0, all-one for symbol 1, and balanced for every other field symbol.
proof_steps.statement: The inner signed sum is `2^15`, `−2^15`, or `0` according as the symbol is `0`, `1`, or neither.

proof_steps.proof: For nonconstant `P`, each of `P` and `P−1` has at most 64 roots in `A`. Constants are checked separately.
proof_steps.statement: Apart from the two trivial values `±2^30`, every Cayley eigenvalue has magnitude at most `2^21`.
Every nonzero codeword has weight at least 535822336.

proof_steps.proof: A degree-64 polynomial with 64 fixed roots can be scaled so that every remaining value avoids 1, because 32704 forbidden scales are fewer than 65535.
Coset injectivity gives `a≥30`; pair counting, 2-adic valuation, and Mersenne divisibility give `a|30` and `s≤30`, hence `a=30` and ambient dimension at most 60.
proof_steps.statement: A relative difference set of size `2^30` in an elementary abelian 2-group has ambient dimension at most 60.

proof_steps.proof: Griesmer plus repeated residualization would yield a `[9,5,4]_2` code; its parity-check columns would be a 9-element sum-free subset of `F_2^4`, whereas translation proves such a subset has size at most 8. Singleton then gives the 1037 product ceiling.
proof_steps.statement: A dimension-17, length-32768 inner/product-distance architecture cannot exceed final dimension 1037.

theorem_statement: The explicitly defined connection set `D⊂F_2^1040` has cardinality `2^30`; its connected bipartite Cayley graph has spectrum `±2^30` together with values of magnitude at most `2^21`, and its binary character code has exact parameters `[2^30,1040,535822336]_2`.
